scope: Source-based review of the corrected existing-Debug LLDB capability-probe method only; no runtime attach, device action, build, or install.
assessment: Using Objective-C runtime lookup is a coherent correction for the Swift expression failure: the cached Expo source gives AppController the explicit Objective-C runtime name EXUpdatesAppController and @objcMembers, DevLauncherAppController the runtime name EXUpdatesDevLauncherController and @objcMembers, and exposes launchedUpdateId/embeddedUpdateId as optional UUID properties. The Debug controller fields are passive optional-value reads. This route can avoid the unavailable Swift module importer without changing app code or build artifacts.

sourceEvidence.fact: AppController is @objc(EXUpdatesAppController), @objcMembers; isInitialized checks only whether the singleton exists; sharedInstance asserts if accessed before initialization.
Debug with USE_DEV_CLIENT initializes and stores DevLauncherAppController as the shared controller.
DevLauncherAppController is @objc(EXUpdatesDevLauncherController), @objcMembers and declares optional launchedUpdateId and embeddedUpdateId UUID properties.
The corresponding optional UUID properties are part of the Objective-C UpdatesInterface protocol.

conditions: Before invoking any getter, verify the Objective-C runtime class exists and the isInitialized class selector is present with the expected scalar Boolean ABI. Call it first and stop unless true.

Only then resolve sharedInstance. Because its Swift return type is InternalAppControllerInterface and the source does not explicitly annotate that property with @objc, do not assume @objcMembers emitted an Objective-C class getter. Require class_getClassMethod/respondsToSelector and confirm its return encoding is an object before calling it; if absent or ABI-ambiguous, stop without substituting another access path.

Check the returned object's exact guarded runtime type against EXUpdatesDevLauncherController before reading anything. Confirm both instance getter selectors exist and have object return encodings compatible with nullable NSUUID; if a selector or encoding differs, stop before invoking it.

Use correctly typed objc_msgSend function-pointer signatures for the class methods and nullable object getters. Emit only initialized/type booleans and the two UUID-or-null values; never dump the singleton or its description.

Keep the scope to the already-running Debug process. Nil Debug UUIDs are a permissible capability result, not Release or embedded-launch proof. Preserve the prior safe process lifecycle: detach in finally, explicitly confirm debugger detached and app resumed, and stop on ambiguity.
Do not call getConstants, manifest APIs, headers, environment or storage getters; do not perform setters, update checks, reload/relaunch, builds, installs, or configuration edits.
risksAndLimits: The previous LLDB attempt proves the Swift module-import path is unavailable in that debugger context; it does not prove Objective-C selectors are callable.
@objcMembers does not itself prove that the sharedInstance property with a Swift-only protocol existential is exported. Selector and ABI preflight is a blocking safeguard, not optional polish.
LLDB expression compilation, Objective-C runtime access, and detach reliability remain untested; this review is not a capability success or Q13 acceptance.
